newsitem.title: USA: Mass gov sees Massport okaying stadium lease - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mass gov sees Massport okaying stadium lease - paper.

text.p: Massachusetts Gov William Weld predicted the Massachusetts Port Authority will approve a plan to lease 22 acres of waterfront property for a new football stadium in South Boston, the Boston Globe said on Tuesday.

The plan, which also includes a restaurant and a National Football League "pavillion, calls for the New England Patriots owner, Robert Kraft, to pay Massport $500,000 a year for the site. And it would be financed with $200 million in private revenues.

Weld appointed the board of Massport, the paper said, adding the lease proposal also needs to get approved in environmental and transportation reviews, and to survive a possible zoning challenge by the city.
House Speaker Thomas Finneran is among those reviewing the bill that crated Massport to see if it has the authority to serve as the developer of a private project, the Globe said.

And counsel for the Boston Redevelopment Authority are preparing to argue the city has zoning authority over a Massport project that is not directly related to the port, an untested legal theory the agency has rejected.
